speaker: Golden-skin
title: Boundaries and toxic associations
text: To folks by no one known house-room deny: - The Vulture housed the Cat, and thence did die. Approach not too friendly to a stranger without reason. In this primal duty of abstaining from injury all Scriptures are unanimous: He who does and thinks no wrong, he who suffers, being strong, he whose harmlessness men know - unto Swerga such doth go.
modern_interpretation: This ancient wisdom advocates for cautious discernment when encountering strangers, highlighting the risk of extending trust or hospitality blindly, as exemplified by the Vulture's fatal mistake. It underscores the psychological importance of setting clear boundaries and not approaching unknown individuals with undue friendliness without a valid reason. Furthermore, it elevates non-injury (Ahimsa) as a fundamental ethical imperative, asserting that those who maintain harmlessness in their thoughts and actions, even when facing adversity, cultivate profound inner strength and attain spiritual harmony or 'Swerga'.
summary: Exercise prudent caution and establish clear boundaries with unknown individuals to safeguard yourself from potential harm. Simultaneously, embrace non-injury in thought and deed as a foundational ethical duty, recognizing that such integrity leads to profound inner peace and spiritual fulfillment.
actionable_advice: Practice mindful discernment by observing and assessing the character and intentions of unknown individuals before extending trust, hospitality, or deep personal connection, ensuring your personal boundaries are respected.
